correctness.rationale: For Gaussian-coprime alpha0=a+bi, delta=c+di with gcd(c,d)=1, F(n)=N(alpha0+n delta), A=N(delta), B=2(ac+bd), Delta=ad-bc and Q=odd(A^2+4Delta^2). If 2 divided two adjacent norms, 1+i would divide alpha0 and delta, impossible. For odd p, p|A and p|Delta would force the isotropic nonzero step modulo p and scalar-dependent starting vector, hence a common Gaussian prime, so gcd(A,Q)=1 and each p|Q splits (p=1 mod4). With D(n)=A(2n+1)+B and 4AF(n)=D(n)^2-2AD(n)+A^2+4Delta^2, the exact p-adic adjacent norm gcd exponent is min(v_p(Q),v_p(D(n))). Thus gcd(Fn,F(n+1))=gcd(Q,D(n)) for all integer n, including zeros. Since n->D(n) is bijective modulo each odd p^e dividing Q, Chinese remaindering gives every divisor and exact fiber weights (p-1)p^(e-t-1) for t<e, 1 for t=e; adjacent D(n+1)-D(n)=2A proves the triple gcd is 1. Separate self-written exact Gaussian arithmetic tests on 20,860 adjacent/triple index pairs gave zero mismatches, but are not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The Magness–Nugent–Robertson source gives primitive Gaussian line definitions and Gaussian-integer divisibility of terms; norm divisibility by a rational prime is a different question because split conjugate factors can alternate. A general resultant only restricts possible primes, not the equality with D(n), complete divisor set, and per-residue exact frequency. Published related SCOPE finite-resultant correction is a different two-variable density theorem and does not imply this one-dimensional complete local spectrum.
